ObjectName.value: Aim fig 4-1-2 induced error in position of traffic

Categories.value: FAA images|Wind diagrams|Air navigation diagrams|Aeronautical Information Manual

ImageDescription.value: (Caption from AIM) In FIG 4-1-2 traffic information would be issued to the pilot of aircraft “C” as 2 o'clock. The actual position of the traffic as seen by the pilot of aircraft “C” would be 3 o'clock. Traffic information issued to aircraft “D” would be at an 11 o'clock position. Since it is not necessary for the pilot of aircraft “D” to apply wind correction (crab) to remain on track, the actual position of the traffic issued would be correct. Since the radar controller can only observe aircraft track (course) on the radar display, traffic advisories are issued accordingly, and pilots should give due consideration to this fact when looking for reported traffic.

ImageDescription.value: An Air Traffic Navigation, Integration, and Coordination System (ATNAVICS) system is staged next to the airfield at Bardufoss Air Station in support of Exercise Cold Response 2022, Norway, March 9, 2022. The ATNAVICS is a USMC expeditionary High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle mounted radar system that provides airport surveillance, secondary surveillance, and precision approach radar. This system allows the U.S. Marines of Marine Air Control Squadron 2, 2d Marine Aircraft Wing, to provide lateral and vertical guidance to an aircraft pilot for landing, until the landing threshold is reached. Exercise Cold Response ’22 is a biennial exercise that takes place across Norway, with participation from each of its military services, as well as from 26 additional North Atlantic Treaty Organization allied nations and regional partners. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Chief Warrant Officer 2 Bryan Nygaard)
